name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightSignedLeafGeneral.meets
theorem_title: Evaluating a signed leaf with arbitrary prefix overlap
natural_language_statement:
Let $f,g$ be integer functions on subsets of a width-$W$ ground set, bounded by $B,D$ through cutoff $c\le W$, with all suffix-transform stages stored. Let stage $s\le W$, prefixes $A,B_0$, and leaf subset $S$ satisfy $|A\cup S|,|B_0\cup S|\le c$. Under the concrete union/lookup/sign/addressing interface, the stated source and Pascal scratch allocations, word bounds for addresses and $(2^sB)(2^sD)$, and depth $d+W+6$, the routine returns the exact signed-leaf value within its stated time and preserves memory below scratch. Prefixes may overlap.

Evaluates the general leaf function used by suffix preprocessing. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Evaluates the general leaf function used by suffix preprocessing. The routine computes both actual prefix unions before lookup, so overlapping prefixes remain within the exact signed-leaf semantics.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightSourceBandBatch.Procs.meets
theorem_title: Constructing every original source-band catalog entry
natural_language_statement:
Let a stored source array have length $n$ and values bounded by $U$, with positive band width $g$, prime control $p$, and residue count $m$. Suppose the source precedes the catalog, the shift is bounded by $D$, and the concrete batch interface, stated space/word bounds, address bound, and five call levels hold. The batch constructs the exact stored source-band predicate for every band in its stated time and preserves all memory before the catalog base.

Builds all histograms and original-index fibers once per source. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Builds all histograms and original-index fibers once per source. The batch retains every completed catalog entry while advancing through all actual bands of the original source.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightZetaPass.meets
natural_language_statement:
Let a width-$L$ subset function $f$ be stored on the compact downset through cutoff $c\le L$, with values bounded by $U$. Fix a coordinate $a$. Suppose source and destination tables are disjoint before mask scratch, all masks precede work scratch, Pascal and powers fit space, the stated address/word bounds including $2U$ hold, the concrete enumeration and cell interfaces are present, and depth $d+L+6$ is available. The routine stores the entire exact zeta step in its stated time and preserves other cells below mask scratch.

Implements a full transform pass over compact enumerated layers. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Implements a full transform pass over compact enumerated layers. The complete downset pass enumerates the compact layers and writes the exact next transform table while preserving the source table.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ThreeSumFastResourcesHybrid.poly_need
theorem_title: Polynomial resources for every fixed hybrid exponent and cutoff
natural_language_statement:
For every fixed pair $k,N\in\mathbb N$, the exact finite-cutoff hybrid resource function satisfies $$\operatorname{PolyNeed}(\operatorname{need}_{k,N}).$$

Ensures both the fast branch and original-triple fallback use polynomial word, memory, and depth resources. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Ensures both the fast branch and original-triple fallback use polynomial word, memory, and depth resources. The finite exponent and cutoff are program constants, so the combined fast and fallback requirements retain a uniform polynomial bound.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBandRawAColor.Procs.meets
theorem_title: Original input to the retained owner and A-incidence catalog
natural_language_statement:
Let $x:\operatorname{Fin}(n)\to\mathbb Z$ be bounded by $U$, let $p$ be a width-$W$ coloring with $n\le2^W$, and let band width $g>0$. Assume the exact ordered reservations for colors, three class segments, normalized arrays and endpoint headers, owner tables, four-cell records, packed incidences, and scratch; the concrete interface and its stated space, word, address, and depth bounds; and the original input segment. The routine constructs its full output contract for the three original color-class lists, negating the third, within its stated time and preserves the input prefix.

Connects actual color extraction and normalization to exact physical owner incidences. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Connects actual color extraction and normalization to exact physical owner incidences. The original color-class witnesses survive normalization, and the resulting owner records feed the packed original-incidence construction.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBoxStages.meets
theorem_title: Construction of every compact box-transform stage
natural_language_statement:
Let $f$ be stored through downset cutoff $c\le L$ on a width-$L$ ground set, with $|f(S)|\le U$. Suppose the concrete size/zeta/enumeration interfaces are present, the $(L+1)$ stage tables precede mask scratch, mask and Pascal scratch fit space, address and $2^LU$ bounds fit words, and depth $d+L+7$ is available. The routine constructs the complete stored box-stage family in its stated time and preserves other cells below mask scratch.

Provides the actual preprocessed box tables consumed by sparse queries. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Provides the actual preprocessed box tables consumed by sparse queries. Every stage is built by the checked compact zeta pass, so subsequent box lookups refer to computed stored transforms.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBoxSum.meets
theorem_title: Summing an explicitly stored family of canonical boxes
natural_language_statement:
Let $Q$ be a subset of a width-$L$ ground set and let a stored list contain subsets $U\subseteq Q$ of fixed size $t$, each with $|Q\setminus U|\le c\le L$. Suppose weights are bounded by $B$ through cutoff $c$, their box stages are stored, the concrete box-query interface and stated data/mask/Pascal allocations and depth bounds hold, and the accumulator bound $|\mathrm{list}|2^LB$ fits a word. The procedure returns the sum of the specified canonical-box values within its stated time and preserves memory below scratch.

Evaluates exactly the supplied canonical missing-set family with bounded signed accumulation. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Evaluates exactly the supplied canonical missing-set family with bounded signed accumulation. The mask list determines the exact summands, and the accumulator-word premise covers their full signed sum.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightLocalCoverSetup.Procs.meets
natural_language_statement:
For natural local scale $h$, assume the concrete local-cover setup interface, its exact layout and word bounds, address representability, and depth $d+464h+8$. The procedure constructs all candidate coefficient/histogram/cover tables, the selected schedule coefficient rows, and the exact candidate index for every schedule occurrence. It returns the schedule-map pointer within its stated time and preserves memory before the base.

Builds the deterministic local cover and its retained data internally. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Builds the deterministic local cover and its retained data internally. The constructed tables retain both candidate histogram orientations and the exact greedy-selected coefficient rows and indices.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightOriginalOffset.Procs.meets
theorem_title: Correct deterministic offset selection from original arrays
natural_language_statement:
Let nonzero modulus $p$ and two original integer arrays have lengths at most $N$ and values bounded by $U$. Assume the inputs end before the free address, the concrete offset interface and stated space/word bounds hold, addresses fit words, and depth $d+\lceil\log_2p\rceil+4$ is available. The procedure returns the exact specified deterministic selected offset in its stated time and preserves the original input prefix.

Implements the balancing choice used before wanted-pair construction. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Implements the balancing choice used before wanted-pair construction. The finite scan returns the prescribed deterministic offset from the actual two arrays while preserving all original values.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightReportingSuffixCell.meets
theorem_title: Writing one lifted suffix leaf cell
natural_language_statement:
Let an interval of width $V$ at offset $o$ fit inside width $W$. Let two subset functions be bounded by $B,D$ through source cutoff $c\le W$, with stages stored, and let stage $s\le W$. For a local subset $S$ within box cutoff, assume each prefix union with its lifted copy of $S$ has cardinality at most $c$. Under the concrete leaf/address interface, stated table and Pascal allocations, word bounds including $(2^sB)(2^sD)$, and depth $d+W+7$, the routine writes the exact suffix leaf weight at the compact rank of $S$ in its stated time, preserving other cells below scratch.

Constructs a physical suffix-local preprocessing cell from the original source stages. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
explanation: Constructs a physical suffix-local preprocessing cell from the original source stages. The local subset is lifted into the original width before reading both source stages and writing its exact compact table entry.
